sections.title: Setup and usage notes
sections.what: Explains what the script does, the rule that delay values are never recalculated, and the two ways to run it: a preview and an execute mode. It also imports the shared helper and its entry type.

sections.name: entries
sections.title: Six dairy plants marked approximate
sections.what: Lists six dairy plants whose stored delays rest on vague dates, each with a note explaining how the date was read. Ends with a comment naming four dairy projects that were left out on purpose, and passes the list to the helper under the dairy audit name.
sections.why: Keeping each judgment beside its data lets the owner check the reasoning.
sections.watch_out: The four excluded projects are recorded only in a comment, so nothing will re-check them automatically.

summary: Marks six dairy plant projects as having approximate delay values, because their planned or actual dates are vague, without changing the stored delay numbers.
purpose: Record that the existing schedule slip values for six dairy plants rest on fuzzy dates, so the app does not present them as exact.
why: The file header says the delay values are guarded and never recalculated, so the script only adds a flag and a note.
how: The file holds a hand-written list of six dairy plants. Each entry has the stored delay, a note explaining the date reasoning, and the three fields that were checked. The list is passed to the shared helper markApproximateDelays under an audit name. Without the execute flag the helper only reports; with it, the helper writes. The helper's exact rules are not visible here.
inputs: A hard-coded list of six dairy project IDs, their stored delay values, notes and evidence field names, plus the database.
outputs: Approximate-delay marks in the database when run with the execute flag. Otherwise, a preview only, according to the header's run instructions.
risks: The values are typed in by hand, so a wrong project ID or an out-of-date stored delay could be marked incorrectly. The notes are judgment calls by the author.
debug: If a project fails, compare its ID and stored delay in the database with this list. Then read the guard rules in the helper file.
